source_use_receipt.actual_source: 1.1 Fix $\theta\in\Theta$. For each $B\in\mathcal G$, the function $x\mapsto K(x,B)$ is measurable and lies in $[0,1]$ by [F2]. Thus its integral is finite and at most $\int1\,dP_\theta=1$ by [F1], [F3], [F8], and [F12]. Since $K(x,\varnothing)=0$ and $K(x,\mathsf D)=1$, the simple-integral formula and agreement [F5, F6] give $Q_\theta(\varnothing)=0$ and $Q_\theta(\mathsf D)=P_\theta(\mathcal X)=1$. [F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, F8, F12]
source_use_receipt.use: Empty action event has mass zero and the whole action event has mass one.

source_use_receipt.actual_source: 2.1 If $(B_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ are pairwise disjoint members of $\mathcal G$, then for every $x$, $K(x,\bigcup_jB_j)=\lim_{N\to\infty}S_N(x)$, where $S_N(x)=\sum_{j=0}^NK(x,B_j)$, by countable additivity of $K(x,\cdot)$. Each $S_N$ is measurable by [F2] and finite-sum closure [F13], and $S_N$ increases. Monotone convergence [F10] and finite additivity of the nonnegative integral [F7] give $Q_\theta(\bigcup_jB_j)=\lim_N\sum_{j=0}^NQ_\theta(B_j)=\sum_jQ_\theta(B_j)$, where the last expression is the nonnegative extended sum [F11]. Together with step 1.1 and [F12], this proves that $Q_\theta$ is a probability measure. [F1, F2, F7, F10, F11, F12, F13, step 1.1]
source_use_receipt.use: Countable additivity together with step 1.1 identifies the action law as a probability measure.

source_use_receipt.actual_source: 3.1 For an indicator $g=1_B$, [F5] and [F6] give $h_g(x)=K(x,B)$ and $\int g\,dQ_\theta=Q_\theta(B)$, so the defining equation for $Q_\theta$ proves the iterated-integral identity. Finite addition [F7] and nonnegative homogeneity [F8] extend this equality from indicators to every nonnegative simple $g$. [given, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8, step 1.1, step 2.1]
source_use_receipt.use: The indicator identity is the defining equation for the action-event marginal; finite linearity extends it to nonnegative simple integrands.
